description: A mathematically-inclined sophomore interested in theoretical computer science who is comfortable with abstract logic but cautious about transition to low-level memory management in C++.

nodes.title: Memory Management & Pointers in C++
nodes.description: Introduction to C++ pointers, addresses, and manual memory management (new/delete) as compared to managed languages.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has no_prior_exposure to C++, they need focused help with manual memory management which differs significantly from Python or Java.
As a student with no_prior_exposure to C++, understanding the distinction between value and reference semantics is crucial for writing efficient code.
nodes.description: Detailed study of pass-by-value vs. pass-by-reference and the syntax of C++ references.
nodes.title: C++ References and Parameter Passing
C++ Class Structure and Header Files
nodes.personalizationRationale: Transitioning from monolithic file languages requires learning C++ specific project structure, which is necessary for students in the no_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.description: The structural basics of C++ files, including headers (.h), implementation (.cpp), and the use of namespaces.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node builds the object-oriented foundation required for all students to implement generic data structures throughout the course.
nodes.description: Implementing polymorphism through inheritance and creating generic code using C++ templates and exception handling.
nodes.title: Inheritance, Templates, and OOD in C++

nodes.description: Implementation of singly, doubly, and circularly linked lists using C++ pointers and structs.
nodes.personalizationRationale: All students must master the pointer-based implementation of linear structures as a prerequisite for more complex hierarchical data structures.
nodes.title: Linked List Implementation and Memory

nodes.description: Assessment covering recursion base cases, stack frames, and the application of Big-O notation to basic loops.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required checkpoint ensures the student can analyze algorithm efficiency and use recursive logic effectively before moving to non-linear structures.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Asymptotic Analysis

nodes.description: Abstract Data Types for Stacks and Queues using both array-based and list-based underlying implementations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: These fundamental sequence structures are essential course content that forms the basis of many higher-level algorithms like BFS and DFS.
nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques
Vectors and the Iterator Pattern
nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding dynamic arrays and standardized traversal methods is a required skill for professional C++ software development.
nodes.description: Exploring dynamic array expansion (vectors) and the iterator pattern for uniform data access in C++.

nodes.title: Bubble Sort and Sequence ADTs
nodes.personalizationRationale: All students must understand basic sorting and the abstract data types that organize sequential information as per the course syllabus.
nodes.description: Implementing basic sequence-based sorting and understanding the Sequence ADT interface.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory assessment prepares the student for the midterm exam by synthesizing concepts from the first three foundational blocks.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment of all material from C++ basics through sequence structures in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Linear Structures & C++ Basics
Tree Traversals and Binary Tree Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: Students must learn recursive and iterative ways to visit hierarchical data, which is a core learning objective of the course.
nodes.description: Recursive algorithms for Pre-order, Post-order, and In-order traversals of general and binary trees.
Building tree nodes and links to represent general hierarchical relationships in C++.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Transitioning from linear to non-linear structures is a required step for all students to understand complex data organization.
nodes.title: General Trees and Implementation Strategies
Heaps and Priority Queue Operations
nodes.personalizationRationale: Learning how to maintain partially ordered data is a required competency for implementing efficient selection and sorting algorithms.
nodes.description: Priority Queue ADT and the implementation of binary heaps using array-based representation.

nodes.title: Hash Tables and Collision Resolution
nodes.description: Hash functions, bucket arrays, and collision resolution techniques like chaining and open addressing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastering the trade-offs of hash-based storage is essential for understanding how modern associative containers achieve near-constant time access.
All students must understand the theory and implementation of self-balancing trees to ensure logarithmic search performance in the worst case.
nodes.description: Binary Search Tree properties and the implementation of AVL rotation logic to maintain balance.
nodes.title: Binary Search Trees and AVL Balancing
Red-Black Trees and (2,4) Trees Concepts
nodes.description: Detailed look at multi-way search trees including (2,4) trees and their relationship to Red-Black tree properties.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This advanced theoretical content is required for the final exam and builds on the search tree concepts introduced earlier in the block.

nodes.description: Applying divide-and-conquer strategies to sorting and comparing Merge Sort against O(n^2) alternatives.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Comparing sorting algorithms is a primary learning objective that tests the student's ability to apply asymptotic analysis to practical problems.
nodes.title: Merge Sort and Selection Sort Efficiency
Final Exam Review: Cumulative Course Capstone
nodes.description: Synthesis of all course topics from C++ basics to balanced trees in preparation for the cumulative final examination.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This final assessment synthesizes all course material to ensure the student is prepared for the high-stakes, comprehensive final examination.
